seoDescription: Transform into the mythical Gorgon with this in-depth Medusa Halloween makeup tutorial. Learn how to create a striking snake skin effect using fishnet stockings and a trio of green eyeshadows for a textured, realistic look. This guide covers everything from blocking out your eyebrows and applying a flawless foundation to drawing dramatic, high-arched brows. Master a vibrant, multi-toned green and purple eye makeup look complete with winged eyeliner and bold false lashes, and finish with a contoured nose and ombre lips.

chapters.title: Building the Eye Makeup Base

chapters.title: Applying Vibrant Lid Colors

chapters.title: Detailing the Eyeshadow

chapters.title: Eyeliner, Mascara & False Lashes

chapters.description: The final Medusa look is revealed, complete with a snake wig and accessories, along with some final tips and well wishes.

summary:
This document outlines the key concepts and techniques for creating a Medusa Halloween makeup look.

## Core Technique: Snake Skin Effect

The signature element of this look is the realistic snake skin texture created on the face.

*   **Tool**: A pair of **fishnet stockings** is stretched over the head to act as a stencil.
*   **Palette**: Use a **dark green**, **medium green**, and **light green** eyeshadow.
*   **Application**:
    1.  Apply dark green to contour areas like under the cheekbones and around the hairline.
    2.  Use medium green to blend over the edges of the dark green.
    3.  Apply light green to highlight areas like the top of the cheekbones.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Do not set your foundation with powder before this step. The tacky surface of the liquid foundation is crucial for the eyeshadow to adhere properly through the fishnet stencil.

## Medusa Face Makeup

### Eyebrows
1.  **Block Natural Brows**: Use a strong-hold glue stick (like **Elmer's Extra Strength**) to flatten eyebrow hairs, then set with a pressed powder. Repeat for thick brows and cover with concealer.
2.  **Draw New Brows**: Create dramatic, **thin, high-arched brows** above your natural brow line using a soft black pencil, then set them with black eyeshadow for intensity.

### Contouring
*   **Cheeks**: The initial snake skin application serves as the cheek contour, using dark green shadow for definition.
*   **Nose**: Use a tapered brush and a **dark olive green eyeshadow** to contour the nose, blending it up towards the purple eyeshadow near the bridge of the nose.

## Dramatic Eye Makeup
This look features a vibrant, multi-tonal eye with a sharp wing.

*   **Base Shape**: Use a fluffy brush with **burgundy and purple shades** to create a defined shape connecting the inner brow/nose area to a dramatic outer V.
*   **Lid Gradient**: Apply colors from the inner corner outwards:
    1.  **Bright Yellow** (or lime green) packed onto the inner corner.
    2.  **Light to Medium Greens** across the center of the lid.
    3.  **Dark Green** on the outer part of the lid, blending into the purple outer V.
*   **Finishing Touches**: 
    *   Apply winged liquid eyeliner.
    *   Line the lower lash line with black eyeshadow, being careful not to cover the green and purple underneath.
    *   Use heavy mascara and apply thick, long, and full **false lashes** (e.g., Bliss #2011) for maximum drama.

## Sinister Lips
The look is completed with a unique three-toned ombre lip.

1.  **Base**: Apply a **black eyeshadow pencil** or lipstick all over the lips.
2.  **Center**: Dab a **blood-red lipstick** (like Rimmel's Bordeaux) onto the center of the lips, blending slightly over the black.
3.  **Highlight**: Press a vibrant **shimmery green eyeshadow** (like Urban Decay's Graffiti) onto the very center of the lips for a final pop.
transcription:
## Introduction & Eyebrow Blocking

Hey everyone, this is my first Halloween tutorial I'll be doing for you guys. It's Medusa, obviously, like the title says. I cover quite a few things in this video so it's probably going to be pretty long, but I really hope you guys enjoy it. Stay tuned.

I'm basically just following Josh's Peacherludes' tutorial on this. I already kind of got started. I just used this Elmer's Extra Strength glue stick, and then right on top of that I just pressed powder using this NYC matte powder foundation. Now I'm going to do another layer because I have really thick brows, and I just want it to be really... make sure that it's covered up as best as possible.

## Applying Foundation & Base Prep

Okay, once you're happy with that, you can continue trying to cover it up even further using like concealer. I'm going to use my Sonia Kashuk concealer, and then I'm going to go over it with foundation as well as apply foundation to the rest of my face.

Blend it down to your neck as well so that just all blends in nicely. Make sure to go into your hairline, onto the ears if you need to. Okay, once you've finished concealing and foundation and everything, don't set your whole face just yet. You want your face to still have a bit of that sticky tackiness from the foundation.

## Creating the Snake Skin Effect

All right, I'm going to grab some fishnet stockings. You can find these anywhere. I found a pair at my local grocery store for like a few dollars. This next part might get a little weird because I'm going to be putting this over my head, but just bear with me.

So I'm going to use a few different green shades. As long as you have like a darkish green, medium green, and light green, that should work just fine. And with this part, you can just kind of have fun with it, put different little patches around your face if you want to.

I'm going to go in with the dark green first, and I'm going to give myself cheekbones. I'm going to go around the hairline area too. Make sure that area is darker. So just kind of going upwards underneath the cheekbone, going around the hairline, around close by the jaw.

Now I'm going to mix NYX Kiwi and Urban Decay Graffiti together, just kind of pressing the brush into both colors. And then I'm going to go overlapping a little bit of the dark green areas and just fading it.

And then I'm going to go in with the lightest green, apply this to highlight some areas as if you're highlighting your cheekbone area.

## Drawing High-Arch Medusa Brows

And we should be good. Let's take it off. Zoom in a little bit closer so you can see. Now we've kind of got like that snake skin type of pattern and effect on the face.

And now I'm going to draw in the high, thin arch brow using this Ardell brow pencil in soft black. Okay, and then I'm going to go right over that with a black powder or shadow. I'm just using NYX shadow in black, slanted angled brush. All right, brows are done.

## Building the Eye Makeup Base

Let's move into the eye makeup, so I'm going to zoom you in a little bit closer. Okay, I'm going to start by priming my lids using Urban Decay Primer Potion.

Okay, I'm going to start off with kind of like a fluffy blending brush or contour brush such as this one. I'm going to go in with this middle burgundy shade right here, and then probably a mix of these two purple shades right here. Just dab the brush in each a few times slightly. And then I'm going to start off by applying some color right here. Okay, just most of the color right under the beginning of the brow, close by the nose bridge area, and just kind of fluff the color outwards this way. And then whatever you have remaining on the brush, bring it down just a little bit.

And I'm also going to apply this shade right in the outer edge of the eye, outer V. Focus most of the color just out here first, deposit all that color. You should feel it sinking right into your eye socket. And then swiftly just blend out the edges. And you can start to slowly just blend it into and connect it to where we left off right here. Okay, so that's about what we want for now. It kind of gives us an outline.

## Applying Vibrant Lid Colors

Now I'm going to go in with a bright yellow. I'm using MAC's Chrome Yellow. You can also use a lime green if you can't find a yellow; that would work just as well. I'm going to start by applying this right in the inner corner of my lid. Make sure to just really pack that on there. Just apply that, blend that into that dark shade a little bit.

To blend it in, I'm going to apply the other green shades, kind of fading it outwards, going with the light green and then the medium green, a little bit of Graffiti—just light to dark. So I'm going to go in with the mix of the light and medium greens and I'm just going to apply that pretty much close to the center part of the lid, just blending as I go. Then I'm going to go into Graffiti, 'cause it's a brighter, more vibrant green, and just blend that in. Then I'm going to finish off with the dark olive green, and that should be blended into the purplish color.

## Detailing the Eyeshadow

I'm going to take a little bit of that dark green and lightly just apply it right on the outer edge of the purple here that we blended earlier. Lightly blend that out. And I'm going to go back with that smudge brush and go back in with the medium greens, and I'm going to have that fading outwards this way. So now it's pretty much going from dark to light. So here's some green.

I'm also going to apply some of that medium green right underneath my lower lash line in the middle part. Go back into your yellow shadow, and I'm going to apply some yellow closely at the top, the highest point underneath our drawn-in brow. And then make sure to blend it into the edges of the green.

I'm going to grab this short shader brush, which is similar to that other brush I was using, and just go into these dark purple colors, just kind of going back and forth here. And I'm going to apply this right on the outer edge of my lower lash line. Be sure to blend that into the green from earlier. Connect it to the outer V area that you have going on here.

I'm going to take some of that really deep purple plum color, and I'm just going to apply it in the outer V area once again just to deepen up this area. I'm just kind of placing the color in right now. I'm going to take the brush I used earlier and just soften that up and blend that in.

## Eyeliner, Mascara & False Lashes

Okay, now we're moving into the eyeliner. Pretty much done with the shadows. I'm just going to use NYC's liquid eyeliner, the black one, and just apply it all across my lash line, thickening up as I go further outwards, and wing it out. Just like that.

Then I'm going to take the black shadow from earlier that I used to fill my brows to just line the lower lash line. Just make sure you don't cover up the other colors that you applied earlier, like the green and the purple.

Now I'm going to curl the lashes, apply mascara before I put on the false lashes. Really pile it on on the lower lashes. And next I'm going to pop on these lashes by Bliss. They're really thick and long and full. These are number 2011s. And definitely wear whatever lashes you want. Have fun with it, go all out. I mean it's Halloween. I would say just if you're going for a sexy something look for Halloween, the lashes will do the trick.

## Nose Contouring & Sinister Lips

I'm going to go in with that olive green color to do the contouring since that's pretty much the color that's contouring my cheekbones. So I'm just using this tapered brush. Just lightly contour this area. I'm going to start off closest by the bottom part of my nose, and I'm going to just blend it upwards and join it with the purple a little bit here. Just very lightly, you don't want it to look too harsh. Bring it down towards the center part of the nostrils here. I'm just going to blend the color outwards like this. I'm going to apply a little a bit on the outside of my nostrils here.

Okay, last but not least, the lips. I'm going to apply this NYX jumbo eyeshadow pencil in black. If you have a black lipstick, go ahead and use that. I'm going to grab a lip brush to neaten this up since it's such a dark color and you want it to be a very defined look.

I'm going to grab this blood-red lipstick, one of my absolute favorite reds. This is from Rimmel in Bordeaux. And I'm just going to apply this on the center part of my lips, just kind of going right over the black towards the side just a little.

Last but not least, to really finish up this look, I'm going to use that fun green Graffiti from Urban Decay. Just grab some into my finger and I'm going to press that right on the center part of my lips and just blend it in.

## The Final Look & Outro

Okay, so let's zoom you out and put on the wig and finish up the whole look. Okay, so this feels really heavy with the big snake, so I definitely would just go with a bunch of small snakes and just work it around your hair. But that is the completed look. I had a lot of fun with this. Oh, I got all these things—snakes, the snake ring, the wig—from a Halloween store, so you should be able to find similar items. But just definitely be creative with it, have fun, have a safe and fun Halloween, and I really hope you guys enjoyed this tutorial. Bye!
